transcript.text: Good to have everyone here. As we all know, the finale goes live this Saturday at 9:00 PM Eastern, and I'll be making the binding call on the final voting package. The current draft has SMS and online portal voting open to our broadcast audience. Before we lock anything, I want to make sure standards, platform production, rights, and data protection all weigh in so we can document the final package properly. Who wants to start?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag something from the network's current standards memo, which I issued after the draft voting rules were circulated. The memo confirms three requirements: voters must be at least 13 years old, each voter may cast exactly one vote per verified account, and voting must close at 9:50 PM Eastern. These are binding standards requirements that need to be reflected in the final voting package.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to share critical findings from the platform certification test I completed this morning. The SMS integration failed certification — it is not approved for use. The web portal passed certification, but there's an important requirement: the approved portal requires account verification before a vote is accepted. This directly impacts our voting package since the current draft includes SMS voting, which we cannot use.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to flag a rights issue with the current voting interface. I obtained the finalist label's written approval today. The approval confirms that the voting interface may display finalist names and approved headshots, but it may NOT use any finalist performance audio or video. The problem is that the current draft interface still contains performance clips, which are not approved. Those clips need to be removed before we lock the package.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I need to flag a data protection issue. My privacy review with the voting vendor, completed this week, established two binding requirements: participation must be limited to viewers physically located in the United States and Canada, and voter identifiers must be deleted within 30 days. The current draft still describes worldwide participation and has no deletion step. Both of these need to be corrected before we lock the package.
